C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:102  TanStack React Query caches the results of your Queries, so using the same Query hook function in multiple places in your application allows the entire application to automatically see updates to that Query's data.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:104  Query hooks execute their Queries automatically when called, and periodically refresh, unless you change the `queryOptions` for the Query. C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:108  ## Using Query Hooks
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:109  Here's a general overview of how to use the generated Query hooks in your code:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:111  - If the Query has no variables, the Query hook function does not require arguments.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:112  - If the Query has any required variables, the Query hook function will require at least one argument: an object that contains all the required variables for the Query.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:113  - If the Query has some required and some optional variables, only required variables are necessary in the variables argument object, and optional variables may be provided as well.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:114  - If all of the Query's variables are optional, the Query hook function does not require any arguments.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:115  - Query hook functions can be called with or without passing in a `DataConnect` instance as an argument. If no `DataConnect` argument is passed in, then the generated SDK will call `getDataConnect(connectorConfig)` behind the scenes for you.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:116  - Query hooks functions can be called with or without passing in an `options` argument of type `useDataConnectQueryOptions`. To learn more about the `options` argument, see the [TanStack React Query documentation](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/guides/query-options).
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:117  - ***Special case:***  If the Query has all optional variables and you would like to provide an `options` argument to the Query hook function without providing any variables, you must pass `undefined` where you would normally pass the Query's variables, and then may provide the `options` argument.

C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:544  # Mutations
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:546  The React generated SDK provides Mutations hook functions that call and return [`useDataConnectMutation`](https://react-query-firebase.invertase.dev/react/data-connect/mutations) hooks from TanStack Query Firebase.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:548  Calling these hook functions will return a `UseMutationResult` object. This object holds the state of your Mutation, including whether the Mutation is loading, has completed, or has succeeded/failed, and the most recent data returned by the Mutation, among other things. To learn more about these hooks and how to use them, see the [TanStack Query Firebase documentation](https://react-query-firebase.invertase.dev/react/data-connect/mutations).
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:550  Mutation hooks do not execute their Mutations automatically when called. Rather, after calling the Mutation hook function and getting a `UseMutationResult` object, you must call the `UseMutationResult.mutate()` function to execute the Mutation.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:552  To learn more about TanStack React Query's Mutations, see the [TanStack React Query documentation](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations).
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:554  ## Using Mutation Hooks
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:555  Here's a general overview of how to use the generated Mutation hooks in your code:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:557  - Mutation hook functions are not called with the arguments to the Mutation. Instead, arguments are passed to `UseMutationResult.mutate()`.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:558  - If the Mutation has no variables, the `mutate()` function does not require arguments.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:559  - If the Mutation has any required variables, the `mutate()` function will require at least one argument: an object that contains all the required variables for the Mutation.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:560  - If the Mutation has some required and some optional variables, only required variables are necessary in the variables argument object, and optional variables may be provided as well.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:561  - If all of the Mutation's variables are optional, the Mutation hook function does not require any arguments.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:562  - Mutation hook functions can be called with or without passing in a `DataConnect` instance as an argument. If no `DataConnect` argument is passed in, then the generated SDK will call `getDataConnect(connectorConfig)` behind the scenes for you.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:563  - Mutation hooks also accept an `options` argument of type `useDataConnectMutationOptions`. To learn more about the `options` argument, see the [TanStack React Query documentation](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations#mutation-side-effects).
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:564  - `UseMutationResult.mutate()` also accepts an `options` argument of type `useDataConnectMutationOptions`.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:565  - ***Special case:*** If the Mutation has no arguments (or all optional arguments and you wish to provide none), and you want to pass `options` to `UseMutationResult.mutate()`, you must pass `undefined` where you would normally pass the Mutation's arguments, and then may provide the options argument.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\react\README.md:567  Below are examples of how to use the `example` connector's generated Mutation hook functions to execute each Mutation. You can also follow the examples from the [Data Connect documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs/data-connect/web-sdk#operations-react-angular).

C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:54  # Queries
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:56  There are two ways to execute a Data Connect Query using the generated Web SDK:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:57  - Using a Query Reference function, which returns a `QueryRef`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:58  - The `QueryRef` can be used as an argument to `executeQuery()`, which will execute the Query and return a `QueryPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:59  - Using an action shortcut function, which returns a `QueryPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:60  - Calling the action shortcut function will execute the Query and return a `QueryPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:62  The following is true for both the action shortcut function and the `QueryRef` function:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:63  - The `QueryPromise` returned will resolve to the result of the Query once it has finished executing
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:64  - If the Query accepts arguments, both the action shortcut function and the `QueryRef` function accept a single argument: an object that contains all the required variables (and the optional variables) for the Query
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:65  - Both functions can be called with or without passing in a `DataConnect` instance as an argument. If no `DataConnect` argument is passed in, then the generated SDK will call `getDataConnect(connectorConfig)` behind the scenes for you.

C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:611  # Mutations
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:613  There are two ways to execute a Data Connect Mutation using the generated Web SDK:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:614  - Using a Mutation Reference function, which returns a `MutationRef`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:615  - The `MutationRef` can be used as an argument to `executeMutation()`, which will execute the Mutation and return a `MutationPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:616  - Using an action shortcut function, which returns a `MutationPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:617  - Calling the action shortcut function will execute the Mutation and return a `MutationPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:619  The following is true for both the action shortcut function and the `MutationRef` function:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:620  - The `MutationPromise` returned will resolve to the result of the Mutation once it has finished executing
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:621  - If the Mutation accepts arguments, both the action shortcut function and the `MutationRef` function accept a single argument: an object that contains all the required variables (and the optional variables) for the Mutation
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:622  - Both functions can be called with or without passing in a `DataConnect` instance as an argument. If no `DataConnect` argument is passed in, then the generated SDK will call `getDataConnect(connectorConfig)` behind the scenes for you.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\client\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:624  Below are examples of how to use the `example` connector's generated functions to execute each mutation. You can also follow the examples from the [Data Connect documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs/data-connect/web-sdk#using-mutations).

C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:52  # Queries
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:54  There are two ways to execute a Data Connect Query using the generated Web SDK:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:55  - Using a Query Reference function, which returns a `QueryRef`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:56  - The `QueryRef` can be used as an argument to `executeQuery()`, which will execute the Query and return a `QueryPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:57  - Using an action shortcut function, which returns a `QueryPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:58  - Calling the action shortcut function will execute the Query and return a `QueryPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:60  The following is true for both the action shortcut function and the `QueryRef` function:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:61  - The `QueryPromise` returned will resolve to the result of the Query once it has finished executing
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:62  - If the Query accepts arguments, both the action shortcut function and the `QueryRef` function accept a single argument: an object that contains all the required variables (and the optional variables) for the Query
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:63  - Both functions can be called with or without passing in a `DataConnect` instance as an argument. If no `DataConnect` argument is passed in, then the generated SDK will call `getDataConnect(connectorConfig)` behind the scenes for you.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:65  Below are examples of how to use the `example` connector's generated functions to execute each query. You can also follow the examples from the [Data Connect documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs/data-connect/web-sdk#using-queries).

C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:609  # Mutations
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:611  There are two ways to execute a Data Connect Mutation using the generated Web SDK:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:612  - Using a Mutation Reference function, which returns a `MutationRef`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:613  - The `MutationRef` can be used as an argument to `executeMutation()`, which will execute the Mutation and return a `MutationPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:614  - Using an action shortcut function, which returns a `MutationPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:615  - Calling the action shortcut function will execute the Mutation and return a `MutationPromise`
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:617  The following is true for both the action shortcut function and the `MutationRef` function:
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:618  - The `MutationPromise` returned will resolve to the result of the Mutation once it has finished executing
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:619  - If the Mutation accepts arguments, both the action shortcut function and the `MutationRef` function accept a single argument: an object that contains all the required variables (and the optional variables) for the Mutation
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:620  - Both functions can be called with or without passing in a `DataConnect` instance as an argument. If no `DataConnect` argument is passed in, then the generated SDK will call `getDataConnect(connectorConfig)` behind the scenes for you.
C:\Users\Jadney Ranes\contabilidade\functions\src\dataconnect-generated\README.md:622  Below are examples of how to use the `example` connector's generated functions to execute each mutation. You can also follow the examples from the [Data Connect documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs/data-connect/web-sdk#using-mutations).
